lines: When concept can impress the self alone,
no other means required — released from bonded
activity, graced by pure knowledge, having taken
the form of the Lord's power, relied on as means,
it brings forth the śākta knowledge.
l4.sanskrit_cite: tatra yadā vikalpaḥ svayam eva saṃskāram ātmani upāyāntaranirapekṣatayaiva kartuṃ prabhavati tadā asau pāśavavyāpārāt pracyutaḥ śuddhavidyānugraheṇa parameśaśaktirūpatām āpanna upāyatayā avalambyamānaḥ śāktaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati

reads_against.argmap: When does vikalpa itself become the upāya? → Self-powered vikalpa = the śākta upāya: no external instrument, power-form as the means itself.
c1_essence: Concept impresses the self unaided → fallen from bondage by pure-knowledge grace, Lord-power-form relied on → śākta knowledge brought forth.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with abhyāsa weight (quiescence as disciplined practice)
